evaluated.name: GrossProfitLowWCAccrual
evaluated.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at)), IND_RANK(NEG(RATIO(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), at))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Gross profitability is the cleanest measure of operating advantage, but it is only trustworthy when it is not accompanied by a balance-sheet buildup of non-cash working capital; profitable firms stuffing the channel show high gross margin plus rising net operating working capital.
evaluated.reasoning: This uses a balance-sheet accrual (change in non-cash current assets less non-debt current liabilities) rather than the cash-flow-statement accrual, giving a mechanistically different measurement of the same credibility concept. The interaction targets firms whose revenue-side profitability is unaccompanied by receivable/inventory inflation.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: ProfitBackedByWorkingCapitalRelease
evaluated.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(oiadp, at)), SUMRANK(RATIO(recch, at), RATIO(invch, at)))
evaluated.hypothesis: The specific accrual channels that most often flatter earnings are receivables and inventory; profitable firms that simultaneously release (rather than absorb) cash into receivables and inventory have demand-driven, sustainable profits.
evaluated.reasoning: Rather than using an aggregate accrual, this decomposes accrual quality into the two components most linked to aggressive revenue recognition and overproduction, and interacts their combined rank with the profitability rank. It should sharpen the separation between durable and reversal-prone profitability, with coverage limited to firms reporting cash-flow statement detail.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: GrossProfitWcapAccrual
evaluated.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at)), IND_RANK(NEG(RATIO(DELTA(wcap, 1), at))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Gross profitability is durable when it is not accompanied by an expansion of net working capital; profits that show up as swelling working capital rather than cash are transitory and reverse.
evaluated.reasoning: This replaces the four-item balance-sheet accrual construction (act, che, lct, dlc) with the directly reported wcap, which should sharply raise coverage from the 11% of the prior winner while measuring the same economic quantity. Comparing its statistics with the archived version isolates whether the prior result was driven by the cash/short-debt exclusions or simply by the working-capital accrual itself.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: GrossProfitAccrualGate
evaluated.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at)), INDICATOR(NEG(RATIO(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), at)), 0))
evaluated.hypothesis: The gross profitability premium exists only in the state where working-capital accruals are non-positive; when profits are accrual-financed the profitability signal carries no reliable information about future returns.
evaluated.reasoning: This holds the underlying variables fixed relative to the archived winner and changes only the interaction form, from a smooth rank product to a hard state gate, so it directly tests whether the effect is a genuine conditional regime or a continuous double-sort. If the gated version retains most of the alpha, the mechanism is state-dependent credibility rather than a linear accrual penalty.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: SustainedProfitAccrualBuildup
evaluated.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(MA(RATIO(SUB(SUB(revt, cogs), xsga), at), 3)), IND_RANK(NEG(TS_SUM(RATIO(DELTA(wcap, 1), at), 3))))
evaluated.hypothesis: What matters is the cumulative multi-year buildup of working capital relative to a persistently profitable operation: firms that have sustained operating profitability for three years without accumulating accruals have genuinely cash-generative business models.
evaluated.reasoning: Single-year accruals are noisy and partly reflect legitimate growth timing, whereas a three-year accumulation identifies chronic accrual reliance, and a three-year average profitability isolates the persistent rather than transitory profit component. This tests horizon as the key design dimension: does earnings credibility operate at an annual or multi-year frequency?
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: ProfitOnHardAssets
evaluated.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(oiadp, at)), IND_RANK(NEG(RATIO(SUB(act, che), at))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Profitability generated on a balance sheet already bloated with soft, estimate-laden assets (receivables and inventory) is less credible than the same profitability earned on a lean, cash-heavy asset base, because accumulated soft assets embed prior unreversed accruals.
evaluated.reasoning: This uses accrual *levels* (stock of non-cash current assets) rather than accrual *flows*, testing the balance-sheet-bloat mechanism in which the cumulative history of accruals, not this year's change, marks earnings that must eventually be written down. It is a distinct economic channel from the flow-accrual signals and should have high coverage since act and che are widely reported.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: BookTaxBackedProfit
evaluated.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(pi, at)), IND_RANK(RATIO(DELTA(txp, 1), at)))
evaluated.hypothesis: Pretax profits are more credible when the firm is simultaneously recognizing a larger tax obligation; profits reported to shareholders but not to the tax authority reflect accrual-driven book income with low persistence.
evaluated.reasoning: Book-tax conformity is an accrual-quality channel that is independent of the working-capital accrual literature, since managers face a real cash cost to inflating taxable income. Interacting pretax profitability with the change in taxes payable should separate profitable firms whose earnings are validated by the tax system from those whose earnings live only in book accruals.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: ProfitPerAccrualInstability
evaluated.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(MA(RATIO(oibdp, at), 3)), IND_RANK(NEG(VOL(RATIO(DELTA(wcap, 1), at), 5))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Stable accrual processes indicate reliable estimation and mapping of accruals into cash; profitable firms whose working-capital accruals are erratic have low-quality earnings whose apparent profitability is partly measurement noise.
evaluated.reasoning: This shifts the accrual dimension from the first moment (level or sign of accruals) to the second moment (accrual volatility, a Dechow-Dichev style quality proxy), which is a distinguishable mechanism: a firm can have small average accruals but highly unstable ones. If it works, it implies the market misprices earnings-quality noise rather than accrual direction.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: SloanTotalAccrualGrossProfit
evaluated.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at)), IND_RANK(NEG(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), dp), at))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Total accruals — working-capital accruals plus the non-cash depreciation charge — measure the full wedge between reported profit and cash, so profitable firms with low total accruals have the most credible earnings.
evaluated.reasoning: This holds the winning gross-profitability leg and the winning ΔWC construction fixed and adds only the depreciation component, isolating whether the long-lived-asset part of accruals carries incremental earnings-quality information or merely adds capital-intensity noise. Because depreciation is mechanically related to asset heaviness, the test also tells us how much of the winner is a capital-intensity effect.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: PercentAccrualGrossProfit
evaluated.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at)), IND_RANK(NEG(RATIO(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), WINSOR(ABS(ib), 1)))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Accrual reliance is best measured relative to the size of reported earnings rather than the asset base: a given dollar of accruals contaminates a small profit far more than a large one, so percent accruals sharpen the separation between durable and reversal-prone profitability.
evaluated.reasoning: The deflator is the single design choice not yet varied in the winning family, and the percent-accrual literature suggests earnings-scaled accruals dominate asset-scaled accruals for identifying earnings that will reverse. Winsorizing the absolute-earnings denominator controls the near-zero-earnings blowups that would otherwise dominate the ranks.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: ProfitWithSalesAlignedSoftAssets
evaluated.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at)), IND_RANK(NEG(SUB(GROWTH(SUB(act, che), 1), GROWTH(sale, 1)))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Accruals are benign when they merely finance genuine sales expansion and malign when non-cash current assets grow faster than sales; profitable firms whose receivables and inventory outrun revenue are recognizing income that has not been earned in cash.
evaluated.reasoning: This benchmarks the accrual buildup against real business activity instead of the asset base, which should strip out the growth component that made the three-year accrual accumulation signal misfire. It is a distinguishable mechanism — accrual/activity misalignment rather than accrual level — and uses only widely reported items so coverage should match the winner.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: CashFlowWCAccrualProfit
evaluated.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at)), IND_RANK(RATIO(ADD(recch, ADD(invch, apalch)), at)))
evaluated.hypothesis: Measuring working-capital accruals directly from the cash-flow statement — receivables, inventory and payables cash effects — avoids the merger, divestiture and reclassification noise embedded in balance-sheet differences, giving a cleaner read on whether profits converted to cash.
evaluated.reasoning: The gen-0 cash-flow-component attempt failed, but it omitted payables, used a plain rank of raw profitability, and used SUMRANK rather than the multiplicative interaction that worked; this version fixes all three while keeping the same measurement philosophy. If it still fails while the balance-sheet version succeeds, the evidence points to the balance-sheet accrual capturing bloat that the cash-flow statement nets away.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: ProfitImprovementCashBacked
evaluated.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(DELTA(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at), 1)), IND_RANK(NEG(RATIO(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), at))))
evaluated.hypothesis: What the market misprices is the quality of profitability *improvements*: a margin expansion accompanied by falling working-capital accruals is real operating progress, whereas the same improvement with rising accruals reflects pulled-forward revenue that will reverse.
evaluated.reasoning: This changes the profitability leg from a level to a change while retaining the winning accrual construction, testing whether earnings-quality conditioning is most valuable exactly when profitability news is fresh. It targets a different investor error — extrapolating recent profit improvements — than the level-based signals in the archive.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: AdditiveProfitAccrualBenchmark
evaluated.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at), NEG(RATIO(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), at)))
evaluated.hypothesis: If cash-backed profitability works only because both themes independently predict returns, an equal-weighted additive combination should match the multiplicative version; if the multiplicative version is materially stronger, the credibility effect is genuinely interactive and concentrated in the profitable-and-clean corner.
evaluated.reasoning: This is the control experiment for the whole research line: same two economic legs, purely additive aggregation, no interaction term. Its relative performance against the gen-0 winner tells us whether future effort should go into sharpening the interaction geometry or simply into better measurement of each leg.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: AdditivePercentAccrualGrossProfit
evaluated.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at), NEG(RATIO(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), WINSOR(ABS(ib), 1))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Durable profitability is best identified by combining a clean asset-scaled gross margin with an earnings-scaled measure of accrual reliance, since the two legs capture the level and the credibility of profit respectively.
evaluated.reasoning: This merges the two independently best-performing design choices in the archive — the additive aggregation that produced the largest FF5 alpha and the percent-accrual deflator that produced the best Sharpe — which have never been tested together. If it dominates both parents, the effect is driven by measurement quality of each leg rather than by interaction geometry.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: CashBasedOperatingProfit
evaluated.expression: RATIO(SUB(SUB(SUB(revt, cogs), xsga), DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1)), at)
evaluated.hypothesis: Instead of ranking profitability and accruals separately, subtract the accrual dollars directly from operating profit dollars: what remains is the cash the operation actually generated, and only that portion of profitability is priced with a delay.
evaluated.reasoning: Dollar netting is a fundamentally different interaction geometry from rank products or rank sums, because it lets a large accrual fully offset a large profit within the same firm rather than trading off two cross-sectional percentiles. It also avoids the double-counting that arises when both legs are already asset-scaled ranks, and should give a cleanly interpretable long leg of genuinely cash-generative firms.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: ProfitWithDiversifiedAccrualQuality
evaluated.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at), SUMRANK(NEG(RATIO(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), WINSOR(ABS(ib), 1))), NEG(SUB(GROWTH(SUB(act, che), 1), GROWTH(sale, 1)))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Two independent readings of accrual quality — the earnings-scaled accrual and the misalignment between soft-asset growth and sales growth — measure the same credibility construct with different errors, so averaging them should reduce measurement noise in the accrual leg without diluting the profitability leg.
evaluated.reasoning: Both accrual proxies individually generated t-stats above 5 when paired with gross profitability, but they load on different sources of contamination (one-off balance-sheet events versus genuine growth financing). Diversifying the accrual leg while keeping a single profitability leg tests whether residual noise in accrual measurement is what caps the current alpha.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: PureProfitAccrualInteraction
evaluated.expression: MUL(IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at), 1)), IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(NEG(RATIO(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), at)), 1)))
evaluated.hypothesis: The credibility mechanism implies a true interaction: accrual quality should matter most for firms with extreme profitability, so the product of mean-centered standardized legs — which is near zero for average firms and large only in the profitable-and-clean or unprofitable-and-dirty corners — should still predict returns.
evaluated.reasoning: Because industry z-scores are centered, this expression contains only the interaction term and almost none of the two main effects, unlike the rank product whose components remain positively signed. It is the decisive test of whether the archive's success reflects genuine conditioning or two stacked single-theme premia, and its answer should determine where the remaining generations invest.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: LaggedAccrualReversalOnProfit
evaluated.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at)), IND_RANK(NEG(LAG(RATIO(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), at), 1))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Accruals reverse with a lag, so last year's accrual buildup — already partially unwound into this year's reported profits — is the sharper marker of profitability that is about to deteriorate.
evaluated.reasoning: This holds both legs identical to the gen-0 winner and shifts only the accrual timing by one year, isolating whether the effect comes from contemporaneous earnings-quality contamination or from the predictable reversal horizon of accruals. A comparable result at the one-year lag would indicate a slow, multi-year mispricing rather than a stale-information artifact.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: ProfitWithSmallAbsoluteAccruals
evaluated.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at)), IND_RANK(NEG(ABS(RATIO(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), WINSOR(ABS(ib), 1))))))
evaluated.hypothesis: What signals earnings credibility may be the *magnitude* of accrual accounting rather than its direction: large negative accruals can reflect distress-driven liquidation of working capital, which is no better a sign than aggressive revenue recognition.
evaluated.reasoning: Every accrual leg in the archive is signed, so we have never separated "few accruals" from "income-decreasing accruals," yet the two imply different economics and different short legs. If the absolute version retains most of the alpha, the mechanism is accounting-noise avoidance; if it collapses, the mechanism is specifically the reversal of income-increasing accruals.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: OperatingProfitEquityPercentAccrual
evaluated.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(SUB(SUB(SUB(revt, cogs), xsga), xint), ceq), NEG(RATIO(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), WINSOR(ABS(ib), 1))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Operating profit measured after overhead and interest and scaled by book equity is a sharper claim on shareholder cash flow than asset-scaled gross profit, and pairing it with earnings-scaled accrual reliance should separate durable from reversal-prone profitability more cleanly.
evaluated.reasoning: The archive has varied the accrual leg extensively but has kept the profitability leg essentially fixed at gross-profits-to-assets; equity scaling changes both the numerator concept and the denominator's leverage exposure. Since the effect is now known to be mostly additive, upgrading the profitability leg is the highest-value remaining lever.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: CashMarginWithLowAccruals
evaluated.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(oancf, sale), NEG(RATIO(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), WINSOR(ABS(ib), 1))))
evaluated.hypothesis: The credibility story is most direct when profitability itself is measured in cash per dollar of revenue: firms converting a high share of sales into operating cash while running low accruals have profits that will persist.
evaluated.reasoning: Replacing the accounting-profit leg with a cash-conversion margin makes both legs cash-oriented but from different statements, testing whether the profitability premium survives when accrual accounting is removed from the numerator rather than only penalized alongside it. Scaling by sales rather than assets also avoids double-counting the asset base that already appears in the accrual leg's economics.

evaluated.name: TripleLegCashProfitQuality
evaluated.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at), SUMRANK(RATIO(oancf, at), NEG(RATIO(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), WINSOR(ABS(ib), 1)))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Profit level, cash generation and accrual restraint are three partially independent readings of earnings durability, and a firm ranked highly on all three is the cleanest example of profitability the market underprices.
evaluated.reasoning: The gen-3 diversification test showed that adding a second accrual proxy roughly preserved performance; this instead diversifies the *profitability* side by adding operating cash flow, which is the direct empirical counterpart of the economic story. If the alpha rises above the 5.4% additive benchmark, the binding constraint has been profitability measurement noise, not accrual measurement noise.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: ProfitWithFirmAbnormalAccrual
evaluated.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at), NEG(TS_RANK(RATIO(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), at), 5)))
evaluated.hypothesis: Accruals are informative about earnings quality only relative to a firm's own normal working-capital behavior; a profitable firm posting its highest accruals in five years is stretching its accounting, whereas a structurally accrual-heavy business is not.
evaluated.reasoning: Every accrual leg so far is cross-sectional, which conflates business-model differences in working-capital intensity with genuine manipulation; TS_RANK converts the accrual into a firm-relative surprise, the poor-man's discretionary accrual. This is a distinguishable mechanism — abnormal versus normal accruals — and can also stabilize portfolio composition by reducing industry-driven turnover.
evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: IndustryNeutralProfitAccrual
evaluated.expression: SUMRANK(IND_ADJ(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at)), IND_ADJ(NEG(RATIO(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), at))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Removing industry means from both legs isolates the within-industry credibility comparison, which is where accrual quality is economically interpretable, and should improve the reliability of the long-short spread by eliminating unintended sector bets.
evaluated.reasoning: The best-alpha signals in the archive use raw cross-sectional ranks while the best FMB slopes use industry ranks, so the role of industry neutralization is still unresolved; this holds legs and aggregation fixed and varies only that dimension. If the alpha holds up with a higher t-stat and Sharpe, the residual sector exposure is noise worth removing in the final consolidation.

evaluated.name: PreferredCashFlowAccrualProfit
evaluated.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at), COALESCE(RATIO(ADD(recch, ADD(invch, apalch)), at), NEG(RATIO(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), at))))
evaluated.hypothesis: The cash-flow statement gives the economically correct measure of working-capital accruals when reported, since it excludes acquisition and reclassification effects; using it where available and falling back on the balance-sheet difference elsewhere yields the cleanest accrual leg at full coverage.
evaluated.reasoning: The gen-2 cash-flow accrual signal had the right sign but only 5.8% coverage, which is precisely the failure mode COALESCE is economically justified to repair here, since the two measures target the identical construct with different reporting availability. Comparing it against the pure balance-sheet leg tells us whether the balance-sheet noise (M&A, currency) is materially degrading the accrual signal.

evaluated.name: IndNeutralCashFlowAccrualProfit
evaluated.expression: SUMRANK(IND_ADJ(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at)), IND_ADJ(COALESCE(RATIO(ADD(recch, ADD(invch, apalch)), at), NEG(RATIO(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), at)))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Within an industry, the firm earning a high gross margin while its receivables, inventory and payables release rather than absorb cash has the most credible profits; industry demeaning removes the sector differences in both margin structure and working-capital cycles that contaminate the raw comparison.
evaluated.reasoning: This unites the two strongest independent improvements of gen 4 — industry adjustment (FMB t of 6.18) and the reported-cash-flow accrual with balance-sheet fallback (coverage 0.121, alpha 4.5%) — which have never been combined. If both effects are additive, this should deliver a high-coverage signal that is simultaneously strong on the cross-sectional and portfolio criteria.

evaluated.name: TripleLegCoverageRepaired
evaluated.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at), SUMRANK(COALESCE(RATIO(oancf, at), RATIO(SUB(oibdp, DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1)), at)), NEG(RATIO(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), WINSOR(ABS(ib), 1)))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Margin level, realized operating cash generation and accrual restraint jointly identify durable profitability; when reported operating cash flow is unavailable it can be reconstructed as operating income before depreciation less working-capital accruals, which is the same economic quantity.
evaluated.reasoning: The triple-leg construction produced the archive's best Sharpe (0.61) but lost a third of the sample to missing `oancf`, so this repairs the defect with an accounting identity rather than a blanket data patch. If the Sharpe survives at roughly double the coverage, the cash-generation leg is a genuine improvement rather than a sample-selection artifact of the post-1988 era.

evaluated.name: IndNeutralPercentAccrualProfit
evaluated.expression: SUMRANK(IND_ADJ(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at)), IND_ADJ(NEG(RATIO(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), WINSOR(ABS(ib), 1)))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Scaling accruals by the size of reported earnings and comparing within industry are complementary corrections: the first asks how much of *this firm's* profit is accrual-based, the second asks whether that reliance is unusual for its business model.
evaluated.reasoning: The earnings-scaled deflator gave the best alpha/Sharpe among rank-product forms and industry adjustment gave the best FMB slope among additive forms, so combining them isolates whether the two corrections address independent sources of contamination. evaluated.name: ConjunctiveProfitAccrualQuality
evaluated.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at)), IND_RANK(NEG(RATIO(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), WINSOR(ABS(ib), 1)))))
evaluated.hypothesis: Credible profitability requires passing both screens simultaneously: a firm is only a quality long if it is profitable *and* clean, while failing either test is sufficient to make it a short.
evaluated.reasoning: Sum and product aggregations both let a strong leg compensate for a weak one, whereas the minimum enforces the conjunction that the economic story actually describes, producing a long leg of unambiguous quality firms. This is a distinct aggregation geometry rather than a re-scaling, and it directly targets the portfolio criterion where extreme-decile composition matters.

evaluated.name: ProfitWithFastWorkingCapitalTurnover
evaluated.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at), NEG(RATIO(SUB(act, che), sale)))
evaluated.hypothesis: Firms that need few dollars of receivables and inventory to support each dollar of sales collect cash quickly, so their reported margins are structurally cash-backed rather than dependent on generous credit terms or channel stuffing.
evaluated.reasoning: This measures accrual intensity as a *stock relative to activity* — an operating-efficiency concept — rather than as a flow, and unlike the asset-scaled soft-asset level tested earlier it is not mechanically tied to the same denominator as the profitability leg. It should be far less noisy than annual accrual differences and therefore have more stable portfolio composition.

evaluated.name: ProfitWithChronicAccrualRestraint
evaluated.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at), NEG(MA(RATIO(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), at), 3)))
evaluated.hypothesis: Single-year accruals are noisy realizations of a firm's underlying accounting posture; averaging three years of correctly measured working-capital accruals identifies chronic accrual reliance, which should be the more durable marker of profits that will reverse.
evaluated.reasoning: The earlier multi-year attempt failed badly, but it used the contaminated `wcap` accrual and a cumulative sum that scaled with growth, so the mechanism was never fairly tested; a three-year mean of the Sloan-style accrual removes both defects. evaluated.name: IndNeutralChronicAccrualProfit
evaluated.expression: SUMRANK(IND_ADJ(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at)), IND_ADJ(NEG(MA(RATIO(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), at), 3))))
evaluated.hypothesis: A firm's chronic accrual posture is only interpretable relative to its industry's working-capital cycle, so demeaning the three-year average accrual within industry should identify persistently aggressive accounting rather than capital-cycle differences.
evaluated.reasoning: This joins the archive's best portfolio construction (three-year accrual smoothing, alpha 5.8%) with its best cross-sectional construction (industry demeaning of both legs, FMB t=6.18), two corrections that address independent noise sources — time-series noise and cross-industry heterogeneity. evaluated.name: ChronicPercentAccrualProfit
evaluated.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at), NEG(MA(RATIO(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), WINSOR(ABS(ib), 1)), 3)))
evaluated.hypothesis: Persistent reliance on accruals is most damaging when it is large relative to the earnings being reported, so averaging the earnings-scaled accrual over three years measures how much of a firm's habitual profit is accounting rather than cash.
evaluated.reasoning: Smoothing and the earnings-based deflator were each individually the strongest choice for their respective metric but have never been applied together, and their combination has a clear economic reading: the fraction of typical profit that is accrual-financed. evaluated.name: DoubleSmoothedProfitQuality
evaluated.expression: SUMRANK(MA(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at), 3), NEG(MA(RATIO(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), at), 3)))
evaluated.hypothesis: If chronic states matter for accruals, they should matter for profitability too: firms with a sustained three-year margin advantage and a sustained absence of accrual reliance represent structurally cash-generative businesses rather than firms enjoying a single good year.
evaluated.reasoning: The gen-5 result showed smoothing helps the accrual leg, but we have never smoothed the profitability leg with the correct accrual construction, so we cannot tell whether the gain came from persistence per se or from accrual-specific noise reduction. evaluated.name: FiveYearAccrualRestraintProfit
evaluated.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at), NEG(MA(RATIO(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), at), 5)))
evaluated.hypothesis: The longer the window over which a profitable firm has avoided accrual buildup, the stronger the evidence that its accounting is conservative and its profits durable, so a five-year average should dominate a three-year average if the mechanism is truly a chronic-state effect.
evaluated.reasoning: This varies only the smoothing horizon, which is the key free parameter revealed by gen 5, and distinguishes a genuine persistence mechanism from mere noise-averaging that would saturate quickly. A decline at five years would indicate that accrual information decays and would pin the optimal horizon for final consolidation.

evaluated.hypothesis: Accrual credibility has a flow dimension (how fast working capital is being added) and a stock dimension (how many dollars of receivables and inventory each sales dollar requires); a profitable firm that is clean on both converts sales to cash quickly and is not currently stretching its accounting.
evaluated.reasoning: The working-capital-turnover stock measure was the highest-coverage accrual proxy tested (0.122) and worked standalone, while the smoothed flow measure gave the highest alpha, and the two are conceptually independent — a slow-collecting business can still hold its accruals flat. Combining them should raise coverage above the flow-only signal while diversifying accrual measurement error.

evaluated.reasoning: Dollar netting is the one interaction geometry structurally different from ranks, and its earlier weak result (FMB t=2.99) plausibly stemmed from subtracting a single noisy accrual realization from a stable profit measure — a mismatch in signal-to-noise that smoothing directly repairs. evaluated.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at), SUMRANK(TREND(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at), 5), NEG(MA(RATIO(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), at), 3))))

evaluated.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at), SUMRANK(NEG(MA(RATIO(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), at), 3)), NEG(DELTA(RATIO(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), at), 1))))

evaluated.expression: SUMRANK(IND_ADJ(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at)), SUMRANK(IND_ADJ(NEG(MA(RATIO(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), at), 3))), IND_ADJ(NEG(MA(RATIO(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), WINSOR(ABS(ib), 1)), 3)))))

Dollar netting was weak as a standalone level signal but is far better suited to a change variable, where the noisy accrual is differenced against its own prior value.

considered.hypothesis: Operating profitability predicts returns only to the extent that reported profits are matched by operating cash flow; firms that are both highly profitable and low-accrual have durable earnings, while high-profit/high-accrual firms are candidates for reversal.

Industry ranking removes sector-level differences in accrual accounting intensity (e.g., capital-intensive vs. service firms) so the interaction is about firm-level earnings credibility.

considered.hypothesis: Profitability is priced correctly only when accruals are non-positive; when cash flow exceeds earnings the profitability signal is credible and the market underreacts, whereas positive-accrual profitability carries no reliable information.
considered.reasoning: The indicator switches the profitability signal on exclusively for firms whose cash flow exceeds accounting income, creating a genuinely conditional (state-dependent) use of the profitability theme. This tests whether the profitability premium is concentrated in the cash-backed state rather than being uniformly present.

considered.name: AccrualNoiseScaledProfitability
considered.expression: RANK(RATIO(MA(RATIO(oiadp, at), 3), WINSOR(VOL(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at), 5), 1)))
considered.hypothesis: Sustained profitability deserves a higher multiple of credibility when the firm's accrual process is stable; volatile accruals (poor accrual quality in the Dechow-Dichev sense) signal estimation noise or manipulation that makes profits less informative about future cash flows.
considered.reasoning: Profitability is smoothed over three years to capture the persistent component, then deflated by the five-year volatility of scaled accruals so that each unit of profit is discounted by measurement noise. This is a genuine ratio interaction: the same profitability level maps to very different signal values depending on accrual quality.

considered.name: ImprovingProfitFallingAccruals
considered.expression: SUMRANK(TREND(RATIO(oiadp, at), 5), NEG(TREND(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at), 5)))
considered.hypothesis: Firms whose profitability is trending up while accrual intensity is trending down are converting improved operations into cash, whereas rising profitability financed by rising accruals reflects loosening revenue recognition or working-capital buildup that will reverse.
considered.reasoning: The signal pairs the direction of the profitability path with the direction of the accrual path, so it isolates the quality of profit improvement rather than its level. Divergence between the two trends is precisely the case where the market misprices earnings momentum.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: GrossProfitLowWCAccrual
considered.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at)), IND_RANK(NEG(RATIO(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), at))))
considered.hypothesis: Gross profitability is the cleanest measure of operating advantage, but it is only trustworthy when it is not accompanied by a balance-sheet buildup of non-cash working capital; profitable firms stuffing the channel show high gross margin plus rising net operating working capital.
considered.reasoning: This uses a balance-sheet accrual (change in non-cash current assets less non-debt current liabilities) rather than the cash-flow-statement accrual, giving a mechanistically different measurement of the same credibility concept. The interaction targets firms whose revenue-side profitability is unaccompanied by receivable/inventory inflation.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: ProfitBackedByWorkingCapitalRelease
considered.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(oiadp, at)), SUMRANK(RATIO(recch, at), RATIO(invch, at)))
considered.hypothesis: The specific accrual channels that most often flatter earnings are receivables and inventory; profitable firms that simultaneously release (rather than absorb) cash into receivables and inventory have demand-driven, sustainable profits.
considered.reasoning: Rather than using an aggregate accrual, this decomposes accrual quality into the two components most linked to aggressive revenue recognition and overproduction, and interacts their combined rank with the profitability rank. It should sharpen the separation between durable and reversal-prone profitability, with coverage limited to firms reporting cash-flow statement detail.

considered.name: GrossProfitWcapAccrual
considered.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at)), IND_RANK(NEG(RATIO(DELTA(wcap, 1), at))))
considered.hypothesis: Gross profitability is durable when it is not accompanied by an expansion of net working capital; profits that show up as swelling working capital rather than cash are transitory and reverse.
considered.reasoning: This replaces the four-item balance-sheet accrual construction (act, che, lct, dlc) with the directly reported wcap, which should sharply raise coverage from the 11% of the prior winner while measuring the same economic quantity. Comparing its statistics with the archived version isolates whether the prior result was driven by the cash/short-debt exclusions or simply by the working-capital accrual itself.

considered.name: GrossProfitAccrualGate
considered.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at)), INDICATOR(NEG(RATIO(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), at)), 0))
considered.hypothesis: The gross profitability premium exists only in the state where working-capital accruals are non-positive; when profits are accrual-financed the profitability signal carries no reliable information about future returns.
considered.reasoning: This holds the underlying variables fixed relative to the archived winner and changes only the interaction form, from a smooth rank product to a hard state gate, so it directly tests whether the effect is a genuine conditional regime or a continuous double-sort. If the gated version retains most of the alpha, the mechanism is state-dependent credibility rather than a linear accrual penalty.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: SustainedProfitAccrualBuildup
considered.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(MA(RATIO(SUB(SUB(revt, cogs), xsga), at), 3)), IND_RANK(NEG(TS_SUM(RATIO(DELTA(wcap, 1), at), 3))))
considered.hypothesis: What matters is the cumulative multi-year buildup of working capital relative to a persistently profitable operation: firms that have sustained operating profitability for three years without accumulating accruals have genuinely cash-generative business models.
considered.reasoning: Single-year accruals are noisy and partly reflect legitimate growth timing, whereas a three-year accumulation identifies chronic accrual reliance, and a three-year average profitability isolates the persistent rather than transitory profit component. This tests horizon as the key design dimension: does earnings credibility operate at an annual or multi-year frequency?
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: ProfitOnHardAssets
considered.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(oiadp, at)), IND_RANK(NEG(RATIO(SUB(act, che), at))))
considered.hypothesis: Profitability generated on a balance sheet already bloated with soft, estimate-laden assets (receivables and inventory) is less credible than the same profitability earned on a lean, cash-heavy asset base, because accumulated soft assets embed prior unreversed accruals.
considered.reasoning: This uses accrual *levels* (stock of non-cash current assets) rather than accrual *flows*, testing the balance-sheet-bloat mechanism in which the cumulative history of accruals, not this year's change, marks earnings that must eventually be written down. It is a distinct economic channel from the flow-accrual signals and should have high coverage since act and che are widely reported.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: BookTaxBackedProfit
considered.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(pi, at)), IND_RANK(RATIO(DELTA(txp, 1), at)))
considered.hypothesis: Pretax profits are more credible when the firm is simultaneously recognizing a larger tax obligation; profits reported to shareholders but not to the tax authority reflect accrual-driven book income with low persistence.
considered.reasoning: Book-tax conformity is an accrual-quality channel that is independent of the working-capital accrual literature, since managers face a real cash cost to inflating taxable income. Interacting pretax profitability with the change in taxes payable should separate profitable firms whose earnings are validated by the tax system from those whose earnings live only in book accruals.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: ProfitPerAccrualInstability
considered.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(MA(RATIO(oibdp, at), 3)), IND_RANK(NEG(VOL(RATIO(DELTA(wcap, 1), at), 5))))
considered.hypothesis: Stable accrual processes indicate reliable estimation and mapping of accruals into cash; profitable firms whose working-capital accruals are erratic have low-quality earnings whose apparent profitability is partly measurement noise.
considered.reasoning: This shifts the accrual dimension from the first moment (level or sign of accruals) to the second moment (accrual volatility, a Dechow-Dichev style quality proxy), which is a distinguishable mechanism: a firm can have small average accruals but highly unstable ones. If it works, it implies the market misprices earnings-quality noise rather than accrual direction.
considered.author: proposer

considered.name: SloanTotalAccrualGrossProfit
considered.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at)), IND_RANK(NEG(RATIO(SUB(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), dp), at))))
considered.hypothesis: Total accruals — working-capital accruals plus the non-cash depreciation charge — measure the full wedge between reported profit and cash, so profitable firms with low total accruals have the most credible earnings.
considered.reasoning: This holds the winning gross-profitability leg and the winning ΔWC construction fixed and adds only the depreciation component, isolating whether the long-lived-asset part of accruals carries incremental earnings-quality information or merely adds capital-intensity noise. Because depreciation is mechanically related to asset heaviness, the test also tells us how much of the winner is a capital-intensity effect.

considered.name: PercentAccrualGrossProfit
considered.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at)), IND_RANK(NEG(RATIO(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), WINSOR(ABS(ib), 1)))))
considered.hypothesis: Accrual reliance is best measured relative to the size of reported earnings rather than the asset base: a given dollar of accruals contaminates a small profit far more than a large one, so percent accruals sharpen the separation between durable and reversal-prone profitability.
considered.reasoning: The deflator is the single design choice not yet varied in the winning family, and the percent-accrual literature suggests earnings-scaled accruals dominate asset-scaled accruals for identifying earnings that will reverse. considered.name: ProfitWithSalesAlignedSoftAssets

considered.author: proposer

considered.name: CashFlowWCAccrualProfit
considered.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at)), IND_RANK(RATIO(ADD(recch, ADD(invch, apalch)), at)))
considered.hypothesis: Measuring working-capital accruals directly from the cash-flow statement — receivables, inventory and payables cash effects — avoids the merger, divestiture and reclassification noise embedded in balance-sheet differences, giving a cleaner read on whether profits converted to cash.

considered.author: proposer

considered.name: ProfitImprovementCashBacked
considered.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(DELTA(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at), 1)), IND_RANK(NEG(RATIO(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), at))))

considered.author: proposer

considered.name: AdditiveProfitAccrualBenchmark
considered.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at), NEG(RATIO(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), at)))
considered.hypothesis: If cash-backed profitability works only because both themes independently predict returns, an equal-weighted additive combination should match the multiplicative version; if the multiplicative version is materially stronger, the credibility effect is genuinely interactive and concentrated in the profitable-and-clean corner.
considered.reasoning: This is the control experiment for the whole research line: same two economic legs, purely additive aggregation, no interaction term. considered.name: AdditivePercentAccrualGrossProfit

considered.reasoning: This merges the two independently best-performing design choices in the archive — the additive aggregation that produced the largest FF5 alpha and the percent-accrual deflator that produced the best Sharpe — which have never been tested together. considered.reasoning: Dollar netting is a fundamentally different interaction geometry from rank products or rank sums, because it lets a large accrual fully offset a large profit within the same firm rather than trading off two cross-sectional percentiles. considered.name: ProfitWithDiversifiedAccrualQuality

considered.name: PureProfitAccrualInteraction

considered.name: ProfitWithSmallAbsoluteAccruals

considered.name: IndNeutralMomentumChronicQuality
considered.expression: SUMRANK(IND_ADJ(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at)), SUMRANK(IND_ADJ(DELTA(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at), 1)), IND_ADJ(NEG(MA(RATIO(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), at), 3)))))
considered.hypothesis: Within its industry, a firm that is profitable, becoming more profitable, and chronically free of accrual reliance offers the most credible evidence of durable earnings, because the margin improvement is verified by cash rather than by accounting estimates.
considered.reasoning: This unites the archive's best alpha driver (the momentum leg, 6.0%) with its best reliability driver (industry demeaning of all legs, alpha t=6.09), corrections that target economic magnitude and sector noise respectively. Industry demeaning of the margin-change leg is especially motivated because margin improvements are strongly cyclical within sectors.

considered.name: MomentumQualityWideCoverage
considered.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at), SUMRANK(DELTA(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at), 1), MA(COALESCE(RATIO(ADD(recch, ADD(invch, apalch)), at), NEG(RATIO(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), at))), 3)))
considered.hypothesis: Using the reported cash-flow-statement accrual where available and the balance-sheet accrual otherwise, averaged over three years, gives the cleanest habitual cash-conversion measure to validate a firm's margin level and margin improvement.
considered.reasoning: The cash-flow-preferred accrual leg is the only construction that raised coverage to 0.122 while retaining an alpha t above 5.6, and it has never been paired with the momentum leg that lifted alpha to 6.0%. If alpha and Sharpe hold at the wider coverage, this is the more robust final candidate because it is least exposed to a particular sample era or reporting regime.

considered.name: MomentumChronicPercentAccrual
considered.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at), SUMRANK(DELTA(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at), 1), NEG(MA(RATIO(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), WINSOR(ABS(ib), 1)), 3))))
considered.hypothesis: Margin improvement is trustworthy only when the firm habitually reports a small fraction of its earnings as accruals, so scaling the smoothed accrual by earnings rather than assets should sharpen the discrimination between real and manufactured improvement.
considered.reasoning: The earnings-scaled deflator repeatedly delivered the strongest Sharpe within each family it was tried in, and this isolates that single design choice inside the current best-alpha construction. Comparing it against Signal 2 tells us whether deflator choice or accrual data source matters more once momentum is in the composite.

considered.name: ProfitTrendChronicAccrual
considered.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at), SUMRANK(TREND(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at), 5), NEG(MA(RATIO(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), at), 3))))
considered.hypothesis: A multi-year upward trajectory in margins is a stronger indicator of competitive improvement than a single-year change, and when it coincides with chronic accrual restraint it identifies businesses whose earnings power is genuinely and durably rising.
considered.reasoning: The one-year margin change added substantial alpha, but we cannot tell whether that reflects genuine multi-year improvement or short-horizon earnings momentum that decays; a five-year trend distinguishes the two. Matching the improvement horizon to the persistence horizon of the accrual leg also makes the composite economically coherent.

considered.name: ProfitWithAccrualDeceleration
considered.expression: SUMRANK(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at), SUMRANK(NEG(MA(RATIO(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), at), 3)), NEG(DELTA(RATIO(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), at), 1))))
considered.hypothesis: Beyond the chronic level of accrual reliance, the direction of change matters: a profitable firm whose accrual intensity is decelerating is tightening its accounting and converting more of each profit dollar to cash, whereas accelerating accruals foreshadow reversal.
considered.reasoning: Every accrual leg tested so far measures a level or an average level, never the change in accrual intensity, so this is a distinguishable dynamic channel on the accrual side rather than the profitability side. It also provides the cleanest read on whether the momentum gain discovered in gen 7 comes specifically from the profitability leg or from any recent-change information.

considered.name: RankProductChronicPercentAccrual
considered.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at)), IND_RANK(NEG(MA(RATIO(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), WINSOR(ABS(ib), 1)), 3))))
considered.hypothesis: The multiplicative form of industry-relative margin and industry-relative chronic percent accruals should maximize cross-sectional slope precision, since credibility scales the profitability premium rather than adding to it.
considered.reasoning: The rank product with the asset-scaled smoothed accrual delivered the best FMB t in the archive (6.10) with a 5.8 alpha t-stat, and the earnings-scaled deflator has improved every additive variant it was applied to, but the two have not been combined. This is the sharpest remaining candidate for a signal that is simultaneously top on the cross-sectional and portfolio criteria.

considered.expression: SUMRANK(IND_ADJ(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at)), SUMRANK(IND_ADJ(DELTA(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at), 1)), IND_ADJ(NEG(MA(RATIO(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), WINSOR(ABS(ib), 1)), 3)))))
considered.hypothesis: Within industry, a firm with a high and rising gross margin whose reported earnings have persistently contained only a small accrual share is the purest case of profits that will not reverse.
considered.reasoning: This places the earnings-scaled deflator — which improved Sharpe in every family it entered — inside the best balanced construction in the archive, the industry-neutral level-plus-momentum-plus-chronic-accrual composite. It is the single remaining untested pairing of two corrections that have never both failed.

considered.expression: SUMRANK(IND_ADJ(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at)), SUMRANK(IND_ADJ(DELTA(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at), 1)), IND_ADJ(MA(COALESCE(RATIO(ADD(recch, ADD(invch, apalch)), at), NEG(RATIO(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), at))), 3))))
considered.hypothesis: Measuring habitual accrual behaviour from the cash-flow statement where firms report it, and from the balance sheet otherwise, validates a rising industry-relative margin at the widest available sample without introducing merger or reclassification noise.
considered.reasoning: The cash-flow-preferred accrual leg is the only construction that lifted coverage above 0.12 while keeping alpha t near 5.7, and combining it with industry demeaning and the momentum leg tests whether the archive's best result is robust to accrual data source. A comparable outcome at higher coverage would make this the preferred final signal on robustness grounds.

considered.name: MomentumProfitAccrualRankProduct
considered.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(SUMRANK(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at), DELTA(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at), 1))), IND_RANK(NEG(MA(RATIO(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), at), 3))))
considered.hypothesis: Chronic accrual restraint should scale the premium on a strong and improving profitability profile multiplicatively, so a rank product of the composite profitability percentile with the accrual-quality percentile should deliver the sharpest cross-sectional slope.
considered.reasoning: Rank products have produced the archive's two highest FMB t-statistics but always with a single-dimension profitability leg, while the momentum leg has only ever been aggregated additively; this crosses the two best design choices along orthogonal dimensions. It directly targets the one metric on which the current frontier signal is not the archive leader.

considered.name: DualDeflatorChronicAccrualProfit
considered.expression: SUMRANK(IND_ADJ(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at)), SUMRANK(IND_ADJ(NEG(MA(RATIO(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), at), 3))), IND_ADJ(NEG(MA(RATIO(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), WINSOR(ABS(ib), 1)), 3)))))
considered.hypothesis: Accrual reliance is economically ambiguous in scale — it can be judged against the asset base a firm operates or against the earnings it reports — and averaging both readings gives a more reliable credibility score while doubling the weight the composite places on accrual quality relative to margin level.
considered.reasoning: Both deflators produced top-tier results but with different metric profiles (assets favoured alpha t, earnings favoured Sharpe), suggesting their measurement errors are partly independent. This also tests the implicit weighting question: whether tilting the composite two-thirds toward accrual quality strengthens or dilutes the signal.

considered.name: CashVerifiedMarginImprovement
considered.expression: SUMRANK(IND_ADJ(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at)), SUMRANK(IND_ADJ(DELTA(RATIO(SUB(SUB(SUB(revt, cogs), xsga), DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1)), at), 1)), IND_ADJ(NEG(MA(RATIO(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), at), 3)))))
considered.hypothesis: The improvement leg should itself be cash-verified: what predicts returns is growth in operating profit net of the accruals that produced it, since an increase in accounting profit financed by working-capital buildup is not an improvement at all.
considered.reasoning: Every momentum leg tested so far measures the change in an accounting margin and relies on the separate accrual leg to discipline it, whereas here the discipline is embedded in the improvement measure itself. Dollar netting was weak as a standalone level signal but is far better suited to a change variable, where the noisy accrual is differenced against its own prior value.

considered.name: ConjunctiveMomentumChronicQuality
considered.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(SUMRANK(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at), DELTA(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), at), 1))), IND_RANK(NEG(MA(RATIO(DELTA(SUB(SUB(act, che), SUB(lct, dlc)), 1), at), 3))))
considered.hypothesis: The long portfolio should contain only firms that clear both hurdles — strong and improving profitability, and chronically clean accruals — because a firm failing either test is not credible regardless of how well it scores on the other.
considered.reasoning: The conjunctive minimum improved steadily as the accrual leg was refined (alpha t rising from 4.35 to 5.20) and it is the geometry that literally encodes the credibility story, but it has never been given the momentum-augmented profitability leg that produced the archive's best alpha. It offers the most interpretable extreme deciles, which matters for the stability of the portfolio evidence.
